A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same ControlAR work with 25 readable pages, including the main text, Appendices A.1–A.5, equations, nine tables, and sixteen figures. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original ControlAR generation experiments and ablations in Section 4, together with additional comparisons, control-strength experiments, and resolution-generation results in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v3 retains the original ControlAR experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix A.2, including quantitative benchmark measurements and qualitative generation examples.

M1.justification: The control encoder, conditional decoding, token fusion, and MR-ControlAR procedure in Section 3 are unchanged. Appendix A.2 already contains the control-strength adjustment and grayscale resolution-control procedures in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K, ADE20K, COCOStuff, and MultiGen-20M for the same class-to-image and text-to-image control tasks. Arbitrary-resolution generation and the appendix test scenarios are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical: ControlVAR in Table 1; GLIGEN, T2I-Adapter, Uni-ControlNet, UniControl, ControlNet, and ControlNet++ in Tables 2–3; and OmniGen and Lumina-mGPT in Appendix Table 9. The conditional-prefilling comparison is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The 256×256 C2I and 512×512 T2I evaluations, multi-resolution sampling, metrics, model configurations, dataset splits, and training settings match throughout Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendices A.1–A.2.

E4.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the same encoder, fusion, and training-strategy ablations. The decoding/prefilling comparison, resolution analysis, control-strength examples, and prompt-control failure cases in Figures 2 and 6–9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting without reported repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Table 1 retains the caveat that ControlVAR FID values are estimated from histograms.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples match. For example, ControlAR's canny F1 score remains 37.08 in Table 2 and its COCOStuff FID remains 14.51 in Table 3. Appendix Table 9 and Figures 7–16 are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), covering autoregressive factorization, the training objective, and conditional decoding, are identical. Neither the main text nor the appendices introduce revised mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient spatial control of autoregressive generation, competitive performance against diffusion methods, and arbitrary-resolution generation.

C2.justification: The explanations of encoder and fusion performance are unchanged. Appendices A.3–A.4 retain the same limitations concerning model portability, simultaneous control images, and conflicts between text prompts and spatial controls.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information remains identical, including preprocessing, hyperparameters, batch sizes, GPU hours, and the eight A100 80GB GPUs. Both abstracts retain the same repository link and statement that code, models, and a demo will soon be available.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Section 2's distinction from ControlVAR's next-scale prediction. The discussion of OmniGen and Lumina-mGPT in Appendix A.2 already appears in v2.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint.' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025', and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Two superscript footnote markers before the introduction are removed; the remaining wording and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The header and arXiv stamp displays change, and removing the page 2 footnote markers slightly reflows the opening paragraph. All nine tables and sixteen figures retain identical formatting and placement; page bodies from pages 3–25 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 updates publication metadata and provides a small typographic cleanup. The scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, so these edits produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
